data.name: Falcons Eye Michael Penix Jr. as Starter Once Healthy After Rough Week 1 Loss
data.summary: The Falcons lost 20-13 to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1, with veteran Cooper Rush going 12-of-22 for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions while getting sacked four times. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported on NFL Network that the team prefers Michael Penix Jr. as starter when healthy, targeting Weeks 2 or 3, though he's cleared physically but still regaining field comfort. Tua Tagovailoa is out with an oblique injury and day-to-day, leaving fans frustrated with Rush and hopeful for Penix ahead of Week 2.

Smith also shared emotional plans to bus about 45 members from his mother's Montgomery church to the home opener against Carolina, honoring her memory after losing her, his grandmother, and father last year.

data.hook: Kenny Albert's calls of 'Achane' during the Saints-Lions game left fans scratching their heads, until they learned it was Etienne's preferred way to say his own name.
data.name: Travis Etienne Jr. Embraces 'Ay-Chan' Pronunciation in Saints Debut
data.summary: In the Saints' 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions on Sunday, FOX announcer Kenny Albert repeatedly pronounced running back Travis Etienne Jr.'s name as 'Ay-Chan,' sparking confusion online as many mistook it for Dolphins' De'Von Achane. Etienne had reclaimed the Louisiana-rooted pronunciation—A-chan or Ay-Chan—during his March press conference after signing with New Orleans, with the Saints issuing an official guide to match. Albert confirmed it on X, and fans like Barstool's Jeff D. Lowe called it the day's biggest surprise, while Etienne tallied 46 yards on nine carries.

data.hook: Da’Shawn Hand, the Falcons' nicknamed 'Kingpin' on the line, played just seven snaps before a torn quad sidelined him for good. It's the latest blow to a defense already fighting through injuries.
data.name: Falcons Lose Veteran DT Da’Shawn Hand to Season-Ending Quad Tear
data.summary: The Atlanta Falcons' defensive line took a major hit when 30-year-old veteran Da’Shawn Hand tore his quad in their Week 1 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, requiring surgery that ends his season. Hand had signed a one-year deal to provide run-stopping depth but joins Jalon Walker (torn ACL) and suspended James Pearce Jr. on the sidelines, with right guard Chris Lindstrom also in concussion protocol. Coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed the news, as the team turns to LaCale London, Brandon Dorlus, Maason Smith, and Gervon Dexter for Week 2. Fans and analysts lamented the early misfortune for a unit desperate for stability.

data.hook: Cooper Rush stepped in for the injured Falcons quarterbacks and faced a nightmare debut, throwing two picks including one returned for a touchdown by T.J. Watt.
data.name: Falcons Stumble in Opener as Rush Struggles Against Steelers
data.summary: In their season opener at Acrisure Stadium, the Atlanta Falcons lost 20-13 to the Pittsburgh Steelers, with backup QB Cooper Rush going 12-of-22 for 143 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, and a league-worst QBR of 2.6. Injuries sidelined Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix Jr. (knee), forcing the makeshift start, while T.J. Watt dominated with two sacks and a 35-yard pick-six that sealed the game in the fourth quarter. The Falcons relied on Bijan Robinson's running but couldn't overcome turnovers and penalties; the team plans to turn to Penix as starter once he returns in Week 2 or 3.
